item.title: Father escapes jail after 3-yr-old son falls to death in Cyprus hotel
item.description: A Cyprus court on Friday ordered a British father to pay a fine but spared him prison after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of his three-year-old son, who fell from a hotel window. Joshua Foster’s parents and other relatives were in court for the sentencing, with some weeping and embracing him after the decision was announced, according to Cypriot state media. The incident occurred in the holiday town of Paphos in July on the family’s first day on vacation. The court heard that Foster and other family members had spent time around the hotel pool before returning to their rooms to prepare for dinner. He then left the room with his son and the child’s grandfather. While they waited for the lift, he placed the child on a windowsill so that he could see a nearby water park, not realising that the window was open. The boy fell approximately 10 metres (33 feet) from the fourth floor. Despite efforts to resuscitate him, the child was pronounced dead at the local hospital. In its decision, the Paphos District Court described the incident as a “momentary error” rather than a deliberate act. Foster’s lawyer had asked the court to consider his guilty plea to the charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act, as well as his clean criminal record and immeasurable personal loss. Speaking to reporters after the decision, defender Alexandros Alexandrou said that the “court accepted this was a momentary mistake, not conscious negligence”, arguing the case never should have gone to court. “This was an unfortunate incident. Any sentence cannot bring justice,” he added. The court imposed a 3,000 euro ($3,370) fine rather than a prison sentence. The offence carried a maximum term of four years. The 37-year-old had been allowed to return to the UK during the proceedings to attend his son’s funeral. The BBC reported that he was from Essex, near London. item.title: Troops kill two Lakurawa terrorists, recover four AK-47 rifles in Sokoto
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have neutralised two suspected Lakurawa terrorists and recovered four AK-47 rifles, eight motorcycles and other items during clearance operations in Sokoto State. The operations were conducted on October 15, 2026, as part of sustained efforts to dismantle terrorist networks and restore security in the joint operations area. The Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. Danja said troops of Sector 2 first made contact with the terrorists at Waria Forest, where they engaged them in a firefight, neutralising one and recovering two AK-47 rifles, two motorcycles and other items. He said the troops subsequently engaged another group of terrorists at Sarma village, neutralising one suspect and forcing the others to flee, abandoning their equipment. According to him, further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of six additional motorcycles, two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 23 rounds of ammunition, one communication device and other items. The operation brings the total number of terrorists neutralised to two, while the recovered weapons and equipment are expected to support ongoing efforts to disrupt the activities of armed groups in the area. Danja said the successes demonstrated the troops’ sustained commitment to dismantling terrorist networks and restoring lasting peace and security across the joint operations area. He added that the Theatre Command appreciated the continued support and cooperation of members of the public. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest security outpost. item.title: Tunji-Ojo praises Tinubu for approving lifetime pay for retired immigration chiefs
item.description: The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo has described President Bola Tinubu as a visionary leader whose policies are intended to have long term and lasting positive impact. The minister said this at the closing ceremony of the Specialised Boarder Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) Training at the Immigration Headquarters on Friday in Abuja. Tunji-Ojo noted that Tinubu under the renewed hope agenda, was building a system that would stand the test of time and be in full effect even after he was out of office. “President Bola Tinubu has never been about the immediate, but the future. He understands that the most prosperous nations do not boil, cook, and eat their seeds, they plant them. “What this president is doing is planting the seed so that there will be abundance for the future,” he said. The minister said that Tinubu acknowledged that he would not be in office forever, but institutions would remain forever and what mattered was what would be handed down through generations. He commended the president for putting an end to backlogs of promotions, noting that no fewer than 50,000 personnel had gained new ranks and offices in the span of three years. “It has never happened before, but Tinubu did it. He also increased the volume of recruitment, where we now have no fewer that 40,000 new recruits at once. “When it comes to salary increment, Mr President has done it. In terms of hazard allowances, peculiar allowance, he also did,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also praised Tinubu for his dedication to the welfare of both active and retired personnel, highlighting the increase in pension of retired Comptroller- Generals of Immigration. “Previously, CGs had a pension of about N130,000, it was not encouraging. But what did the president do? He signed, and approved salary for life for CGs and DCGs. “This president has cared for the services more than any president in the history of Nigeria. He has given you his all. “And all he asks from us in the service is to do our jobs well and make Nigerians happy. Everything we have asked of him, he has done. This the least we can do,” he added. item.title: Police debunk report of woman cutting off husband’s manhood in Taraba
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Police Command has debunked a viral social media report alleging that a 24-year-old woman, identified as Maimuna, severed her 30-year-old husband’s manhood, leading to his death in Maigoje village, Gashaka Local Government Area of the state. The command said preliminary verification by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Gashaka Division did not establish that the alleged incident occurred. In a statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, said inquiries conducted in Maigoje village, Mai Idanu Ward and neighbouring communities found no evidence to substantiate the report. According to the police, community members and local leaders contacted during the investigation also did not confirm the allegations. The statement read, “The Taraba State Police Command has noted a publication circulating on social media alleging that a woman identified as Maimuna inflicted injuries on her husband, Haruna Ishaka, resulting in his death in Maigoje Village, Mai Idanu Ward, Gashaka LGA. “In response, the Divisional Police Officer, Gashaka Division, conducted an on-the-ground verification exercise and made inquiries within the area and surrounding communities. “The exercise did not establish the occurrence of the alleged incident, and the communities contacted did not confirm the claims. “Based on the findings, the Command has no confirmed information substantiating the report as circulated. Members of the public are therefore advised not to treat the allegations as established facts.” The Commissioner of Police urged journalists, social media influencers and members of the public to exercise restraint and verify sensitive security-related reports through official law enforcement channels before publishing or sharing them. Ogbeghagha also warned against the deliberate fabrication and dissemination of unverified information capable of causing public disquiet or damaging individuals’ reputations. He said anyone found knowingly spreading false information would face appropriate legal consequences. The command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and maintaining public order in Taraba State, urging residents to report genuine security concerns to the nearest police station. item.title: Arsenal to retake team photo with Saliba after defender’s omission — Arteta
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that the club will take a new team photograph featuring William Saliba after the defender was surprisingly left out of the official 2026/27 picture published this week. According to Sky Sports, Arteta said the original photo was arranged to meet commercial commitments after earlier attempts had been cancelled, and confirmed Saliba was “completely fine” about missing it, after being unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment. The omission surprised supporters, particularly because Saliba remains a key member of the squad. The 25-year-old has yet to play this season because of a back injury, but has made 184 appearances for Arsenal. “We will have another picture with the whole family,” Arteta said ahead of Arsenal’s trip to Nottingham Forest. “Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we’ll announce that as well.” The Arsenal boss said Saliba had been unable to attend and had taken the situation in good humour, despite some banter from teammates. The club plans to arrange a new photograph with the full squad. Saliba has resumed training on the grass as he continues his recovery. Arteta said the defender is progressing well and is due to have another MRI scan next week to assess the healing process. “Every sign so far has been very, very positive,” Arteta said. “It will be good to have him.” Arteta also said Martin Zubimendi could return against Forest after picking up an injury during the warm-down following the Leeds match. Piero Hincapie is expected to be out for another one or two weeks, while Christos Tzolis is making good progress from a hamstring injury sustained on international duty with Greece. item.title: Gov Fubara Rewards Real Madrid Academy Players, Officials With ₦50 Million After UK Tour
item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has awarded ₦50 million to players and coaches of the state-sponsored Real Madrid Academy following their participation in an international football tour of Southampton, United Kingdom. Governor Fubara announced the reward when the academy’s management, officials and players visited him at Government House in Port Harcourt to present a trophy they won during the tour. The delegation comprised 60 students and 12 staff members who participated in the international football engagement, providing the young players with an opportunity to develop their skills, gain international exposure and experience football beyond their immediate environment. The governor commended the academy’s management and officials for their commitment to nurturing young talents, while particularly applauding the students for their discipline and good conduct throughout the trip. The governor commended the academy’s management and officials for their commitment to nurturing young talents. Fubara acknowledged that the academy, which combines academic education with structured football training, was established by his predecessor. He, however, stressed that his administration would sustain the initiative, explaining that the continuity of beneficial programmes should not be determined by who initiated them. He said his commitment was to policies and projects capable of improving the socio-economic well-being of the people, irrespective of the administration under which they began. The governor also pledged to immediately commence efforts to address the academy’s infrastructure and funding challenges, assuring the management that the government would work towards creating a more conducive environment for the students to pursue their academic and sporting ambitions. Governor Fubara urged the young players to take both their education and football training seriously, noting that while professional football offers significant financial opportunities, academic qualifications remain important for their future. He highlighted the enormous economic potential of the global football industry, encouraging the students to recognise the opportunities available to talented players who combine discipline, hard work and determination. item.title: Hardship: Ulasi says opposition failing to win voters’ support
item.description: *Predicts Obi could defeat Tinubu in Lagos By Juliet Umeh A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Dan Ulasi, has said opposition parties are failing to turn Nigerians’ concerns over the rising cost of living into political support, despite public frustration over food prices and the cost of petrol. Ulasi also predicted that National Democratic Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, could defeat President Bola Tinubu in Lagos in the 2027 general election. Speaking on Arise Television’s Morning Show, Ulasi said the opposition had not effectively made its case to Nigerians or presented clear alternatives to the policies of the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government. “There are a lot of things to exploit, but whether they’re effectively doing it is another question,” he said. Asked whether opposition parties were making the most of public dissatisfaction, Ulasi replied: “I don’t think they’re effectively doing it. I’m going to be honest to myself.” He said opposition candidates and party leaders should be holding town hall meetings across the country to explain their plans and engage voters. “You would at this point be seeing town hall meetings from zone to zone. I don’t see it happening. Nigerians are waiting for such information to feed us, and they’re not doing it.” Ulasi said the opposition was more divided than it had been ahead of the 2023 election, making it harder to challenge an incumbent president with access to state resources. “As things are on the ground, it will take some magic for anybody to stop Tinubu. The opposition is still fragmented now, worse than it was in 2023.” The PDP chieftain, who said he supports Obi, argued that the former Anambra State governor could make strong gains in several parts of the country, including Lagos, where Tinubu served as governor before becoming president. “This time around, he will beat Tinubu in Lagos State,” Ulasi said. He argued that voters in the state were questioning what they had gained from having a former Lagos governor as president. “The Lagos people, whether Yoruba or not, cannot tell you exactly that this is our son who has been president and what they have profited from it,” he said. Ulasi challenged Tinubu to hold town hall meetings across the country and explain his administration’s record to voters. “I want him to have a town hall meeting, zone to zone, telling every zone in this country what his government has done,” he said. He said Nigerians would have to protect their votes, while stressing that a fair election would be necessary for voters’ preferences to determine the outcome. “If there is a free and fair vote in this country, Peter Obi will make less than 50 per cent of votes in most states in the North,” he said. Ulasi added that the opposition’s prospects would depend not only on public dissatisfaction with the government, but also on whether its parties could organise effectively and offer voters a credible alternative. item.title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison
item.description: Disgraced music producer Sean “Diddy” Combs, who was sentenced for prostitution-related crimes, has been transferred to a new US prison following media reports detailing an alleged brawl and special treatment behind bars. The 56-year-old was moved from the Fort Dix lockup in New Jersey to Allenwood Low in neighbouring Pennsylvania, a Bureau of Prisons spokeswoman told AFP on Friday. Both are low-security federal prisons for male offenders, but Allenwood Low has a population of around 1,000 compared to roughly 4,000 at Fort Dix. US media has reported that Combs was treated at a hospital for a head injury following a fight with another prisoner last weekend. And in September, NBC News reported that Combs enjoyed a relatively lavish lifestyle at Fort Dix, with access to contraband cellphones and liquor. The outlet also said Combs had men cooking and cleaning for him, as well as someone to give him Chinese-style massages. The Bureau of Prisons did not explain why Combs was transferred to the new prison. “For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, including reasons for transfer,” a spokeswoman said. Combs was sentenced in 2025 after a salacious trial that detailed the alleged “freak-offs” he organised: sexual marathons involving hired male escorts and his ex-girlfriend Casandra Ventura and another unidentified woman. He was acquitted by a jury of the most serious charges against him — sex trafficking and racketeering — but convicted of two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution. Combs is due to be released from prison in March 2028. AFP The post Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bellingham agrees new deal at Real Madrid
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has agreed a new five-year contract that would keep him at the club until 2031, Sky Sports reports, citing Spanish newspaper AS. The reported agreement would extend the England international’s current deal, which is due to expire in 2029. The 23-year-old is also expected to receive improved terms after negotiations began towards the end of last season. According to AS, Bellingham feels at home in Madrid, feels increasingly connected to Real Madrid and life in the Spanish capital, while the club’s supporters value his commitment and influence on the pitch. Since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, Bellingham has emerged as a potential leader in a Real Madrid dressing room adjusting to the departures of influential figures such as Dani Carvajal, Luka Modrić and Toni Kroos. According to the report, the club are seeking a visible figurehead capable of taking on some of the leadership those veteran players provided. He joined Real from Borussia Dortmund in 2023 in a deal that could rise to £115 million. Since then, he has helped the Spanish club win the Champions League and LaLiga. Bellingham has scored three goals and provided three assists in eight league appearances this season, with Real now managed by Jose Mourinho, who took charge in the summer. Bellingham’s importance has grown under Mourinho, whose arrival has returned the midfielder to a role he is comfortable in: operating behind Kylian Mbappé with freedom to move across the pitch. The report also highlights his work without the ball, including initiating the press and contributing defensively. His performances at the World Cup have also strengthened his standing with England. After previously having difficulties under Thomas Tuchel, he has become a key player for the national side and scored eight goals at the tournament. The reported agreement for a new deal follows Vinicius Junior’s recent contract renewal. The Brazilian forward signed a new six-year deal after attracting interest from Arsenal in the summer. item.title: Nigeria had records of only 40,000 expatriates when we took over – Tunji-Ojo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has disclosed that when he assumed office about three years ago, official records showed only about 40,000 expatriates working in Nigeria, a figure he said was impossible for a country of 200 million people. He spoke on Friday at the closing of a training on border control and immigration management for officers of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS. “We got into a system where, by official records, we had maybe about 40,000 foreigners or whatever working in Nigeria. In a country of 200 million, that is not possible anywhere in the world. “And when you do not have the data of those foreigners residing in your country, then how do you manage their affairs? How do you monitor them? How do you monitor someone that you don’t even know exists?” He queried. Tunji-Ojo recalled that the ministry was then overseeing “an agency that should be technologically driven,” but “that wasn’t the case.” He said the ministry decided that “Nigeria cannot continue to be at the mercy of inefficiency.” According to him, the answer was to build what he called the Centralised Interior Management and Administration System, which is bringing the records of the correctional and fire services, and civil defence, into one portal. “Harmonisation of data, strategic handshake of data generating and processing agencies is the only way to have a single point of truth,” he said. He said the reform had ended the problem of multiple identities. “We had people then, one person with two, three different passports. But today, that is history,” he said. The minister said the NIS “of today is one of the most technologically advanced immigration services in the world.” He added that the ministry now has a 10-year technology roadmap and a data centre of “over eight petabytes,” which he described as one of the biggest in Africa, with its command and control centre running completely off-grid on solar power. Tunji-Ojo also had a warning for technology vendors. “Any vendor that is not ready to transfer knowledge to you has no place in the Ministry of Interior,” he said. Earlier, Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nanna Nandap, said the Border Management Information System BMIS now holds over 15 million migration records, but “that number is not the achievement.” She told the graduating officers that technology would not replace their judgement. “An alert is not a verdict,” she said. Nandap set five standards for the officers, which she described as “non-negotiable”: accuracy, integrity, judgment, readiness and accountability. On integrity, she said: “Do not share your credentials. Do not search records out of curiosity. Never use this platform to grant favours, or to settle scores, or to facilitate improper passage. Any such abuse will be investigated and punished.” She said the programme would be judged by its results. “We will judge this programme by outcomes, not ceremonies,” Nandap said. item.title: 2027: Hashim Movement targets 3m votes in South-West
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe The South-West Coordinator of the Gbenga Hashim Solidarity Movement (GHSM), Alhaji Abass Olaniyi, says the movement is targeting more than three million votes for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across the region in the 2027 general election. Olaniyi said the target was based on the movement’s internal assessment of its grassroots mobilisation prospects across the six South-West states, with Osun, Lagos and Oyo expected to account for a significant share of the projected votes. According to him, Osun State is projected to contribute more than one million votes, while Lagos and Oyo are expected to deliver a combined 1.5 million votes. He said Ogun, Ondo and Ekiti states would contribute the remaining votes needed to achieve the regional target. Olaniyi expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to expand its grassroots presence through engagement with community leaders, youth groups, political stakeholders and local organisations across the region. He also said the movement expected voters in Osun to make independent choices in the presidential election, irrespective of political alignments involving state-level leaders. The coordinator’s projection comes amid preparations by political parties and support groups for the 2027 general election. GHSM said it intended to translate its mobilisation efforts across the South-West into electoral support for Olawepo-Hashim and the Accord Party. item.title: Lack of forensic labs frustrating rape cases in Jigawa — NBA
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Jigawa State branch, has raised concerns over the lack of forensic laboratories in the state, saying the gap is undermining efforts to secure convictions in rape and other sexual violence cases. The chairman of the association, Barrister Hamza Umar, raised the concern at a two-day policy dialogue organised by the CLEEN Foundation, with support from the Norwegian Embassy in Nigeria, in Dutse, the state capital. Umar said the absence of forensic facilities had made it difficult for prosecutors to obtain scientific evidence required to establish rape allegations in court. “We cannot secure conviction when we have no forensic lab to prove rape cases scientifically. The law requires forensic evidence. We are still relying on mere confessional statements, which the court may reject,” he said. He also criticised the alleged failure to publish the names of convicted rapists as provided for under the state’s Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Law, saying the provision had not been implemented. The VAPP Law, signed on February 24, 2021, was introduced to address rape, sexual and gender-based violence, physical abuse and other harmful practices. At the dialogue, stakeholders called for the establishment of at least five Sexual Assault Referral Centres across the state’s five emirate zones to improve support for survivors and access to justice. They also expressed concern that cultural and religious beliefs continued to discourage victims from reporting sexual violence, while some families preferred to settle cases outside the formal justice system. Earlier, the Senior Programme Officer of the CLEEN Foundation, Olaniyi Olumayowa, said the dialogue was aimed at addressing gaps between the enactment of the VAPP Law and its implementation. He explained that the law was designed not only to punish offenders but also to protect survivors, provide compensation and ensure accountability among relevant institutions. Olumayowa urged the Jigawa State Government to provide adequate funding for forensic laboratories, establish additional referral centres and train personnel responsible for implementing the law. item.title: ICPC seeks public support against vote buying in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has called for collective action by government institutions and members of the public to curb vote buying and selling ahead of the 2027 general elections in Jigawa State. The Resident Anti-Corruption Commissioner overseeing Kano and Jigawa states, Ahmad Muhammad Wada, made the call during a courtesy visit to the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Malam Bala Ibrahim. Wada said public cooperation was essential to preventing electoral corruption and ensuring credible elections. He explained that the commission was intensifying efforts to tackle electoral malpractices through enforcement, preventive measures, public enlightenment and education. According to him, the visit was part of the ICPC’s public enlightenment campaign aimed at strengthening collaboration with relevant stakeholders in the fight against corruption. The commissioner stressed that addressing vote buying and selling required the active involvement of government institutions and citizens. He reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to combating electoral offences and promoting credible elections ahead of the 2027 polls. Responding, the Secretary to the Jigawa State Government, Bala Ibrahim, assured the commission of the state government’s support and cooperation in tackling electoral offences. He said the government was ready to work closely with the ICPC to discourage vote buying, vote selling and other forms of electoral corruption ahead of the general elections. item.title: Man City charges: Maresca says club, players, fans are ‘more together’
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says he feels no stress over the club’s financial charges, insisting the controversy has brought the club, team and supporters closer together. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday’s clash with Ipswich, Maresca said City were focused on their performance and could not control the debate surrounding the case. An independent commission found the club guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules; City deny wrongdoing and have appealed the decision. “Since the noise, from my personal point of view, I can see the fans, the club, the team more together, for sure,” Maresca said. City have won at Anfield since the verdict was announced but lost to Paris Saint-Germain in a midweek Champions League match. Maresca said the players’ response had been positive and described Saturday’s game as another opportunity to collect three points and extend their winning run. “There is noise around the club but we need to try to make our noise. That means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow against Ipswich,” he said. “This is the way we can make our noise. A different kind of noise; we’re not able to control that.” Asked how he was coping with the situation, Maresca said: “I’m very happy. I don’t feel any kind of stress about the outside situation because it’s something I don’t control.
